terms.register: vōx prīsca et poētica: Plaut., Cato; Hor., Juv.
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 2.6.6: tēmētī nihil allātum intellegō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Any intoxicating drink, wine or mead (Lewis & Short). The everyday classical way to speak of drinking is simply vīnum (see wine); one who drinks none is abstēmius.

terms.gloss: alcohol, the substance (in drinks, for cleaning wounds)
evidence: M-O s.v. alcohol: alcohol, masculine, from 1846
terms.comment: For the substance itself, as in a disinfectant or on a label. Traupman makes it neuter, Morgan–Owens masculine (alcohol absolūtus); we follow Traupman. Neither marks the vowels, and we leave them unmarked.

evidence: Ov. Met. 15.323: vīna fugit gaudetque merīs abstēmius undīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Formed like tēmētum and tēmulentus (drunk); in Horace more generally sober, frugal (Ep. 1.12.7).

terms.gloss: spirit of wine: distilled alcohol, ethanol
terms.comment: The older chemists’ name, from 1826 in Morgan–Owens.

phrases.english: I don’t drink alcohol: I’m teetotal.

sources: Lewis & Short: temetum · Lewis & Short: abstemius · Lewis & Short: spiritus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 70, 270.
